_what: Reproduction of the owner's loop defect: 'once I go through the other side, I stay on plane b and continue to fall through collision on plane A, which is most of the collision, and there's no easy way to get back'.

_build.note: server ROM byte-compared against disk before any measurement; a stale 741905-byte image was reloaded first

_method.instrument: record-mode write watchpoint on Sst.layer at $FF902B (player base $FF8FFE + $2D)
_method.why_watchpoint: a per-frame sampled read under-samples: an 8px cell is crossed in under one frame at gsp $600. The watchpoint records EVERY write, so the toggle count is exact rather than sampled.
_method.placement_rule: camera written and settled 12 frames BEFORE the player, or the player lands outside the streamed collision cache
_method.debug_exit: emulator/press b — NEVER by writing debug_flag ($FF903A), which skips Player_DebugExit and leaves mappings on Map_TestObj (address error in RefreshSpritePieceCount)

runs.label: leftward entry — THE OWNER'S DIRECTION

crossover_writes.note: x 1151 is the loop's bottom-CENTRE (void centre x 1148), not an arc foot

runs.verdict: ODD. Exits on plane B. y 829 is 253px BELOW ground_solid_y 576 — he fell through plane-A collision, exactly as reported.

runs.label: rightward entry

speed_collapse.note: 9px of travel in 18 frames — this is the 'can't get past it coming from the left' complaint

runs.verdict: ODD. Crosses to B and then STALLS on the arc at gsp $8E. Never reaches the top-centre mark.

runs.label: rightward from x 1070 — DISCARDED as a control
runs.why_discarded: he fell before reaching the mark, so the zero is 'never arrived', not 'arrived and did not fire'. Run B replaced it with a grounded pass. Recorded so the discard is visible rather than silent.

static_check.shipped_table: 256 slots, 2 marked, 0 holding the reserved value 3
static_check.consumption: proven by the gate: 2 marks changed Sst.layer BECAUSE a CrossoverTable byte changed and nothing else did; the unmodified table is the control
static_check.meaning: BOTH marks are present in the ROM and BOTH are consumed. The defect is NOT a missing or unbaked mark.

finding.measured: Every traversal tested toggles the layer exactly ONCE, in both directions. The player therefore always ends on plane B, which carries only ground + the RIGHT half; plane A carries most of the collision, so he falls through everything.
finding.primary_defect: The bottom-centre mark is plane-keyed, not direction-keyed (rule R2 raises on self-marks, so a plane-A player reads XOVER_TO_B regardless of travel direction). A LEFTWARD traveller therefore crosses to B at the bottom centre and immediately has no left arc to stand on, because the left half is solid only on A.
finding.secondary_defect: Rightward entry bleeds gsp $600 -> $FC over 18 frames and stalls on the arc, so it never reaches the top-centre mark either. This is the owner's original screenshot complaint.
finding.not_yet_established: Whether a traversal at a speed high enough to survive the arc reaches the top-centre mark and toggles back. No run in this set completed a circuit, so the second mark has never been observed firing.
